**Area:** [Web, network & communication](../COVERAGE.md#web) · **Apple:** [Network](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/network) · **Issues:** [`area:web`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Aweb)

## How isim implements it

- **Passthrough:** host sockets, with the host's OpenSSL for TLS and isim's own mDNS. QUIC is a stub (the host's OpenSSL 3.0 has no QUIC).
- **Adapted:** reports measure what isim's sockets see; application services are Bonjour services of the app's own type; privacy contexts and proxies are kept with the parameters.

Tested (swift-network `nwAPIChecks`, `nwConnectionGroupChecks`) |
| Network's C API (`nw_endpoint_*`, `nw_parameters_*` with `NW_PARAMETERS_DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION` / `NW_PARAMETERS_DISABLE_PROTOCOL`, TCP/UDP options, `nw_connection_*` with `dispatch_data_t` send/receive and content contexts (`NW_CONNECTION_*_CONTEXT`, `NW_CONNECTION_SEND_IDEMPOTENT_CONTENT`), `nw_error_*`, `nw_listener_*` with Bonjour advertising (`nw_advertise_descriptor_*`), `nw_browser_*` / `nw_browse_descriptor_*` / `nw_browse_result_*`, `nw_path_monitor_*`, `nw_retain` / `nw_release`) from C, Objective-C and Swift | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the functions forward to isim's `NWConnection`, `NWListener`, `NWBrowser` and `NWPathMonitor` (so the same sockets, OpenSSL TLS and Bonjour); the objects are Objective-C objects (ARC retains them), handlers run in order on the queue set with `nw_*_set_queue`, and a connection or listener with a state handler stays alive until it is cancelled, as on Apple platforms. Swift sees them as Apple's module does (`OS_nw_*` protocols, `nw_*_t`, the C enums as structs); there the queue setters take a `DispatchQueue` and `dispatch_data_t` is isim's C type (isim's Dispatch has no `__DispatchData`). Not yet from C: the `sec_protocol_options_*` functions (TLS checks the host's CA store and the host name), protocol stacks, privacy contexts and ethernet channels (types only). Tested (HelloSystemObjC: a Bonjour-advertised echo listener, a browser that finds it, a connection that echoes, TLS failing against the plain server, tests/ui/test_system_objc.py; HelloConnections from Swift, tests/ui/test_connections.py) |

QUIC options and metadata are kept (no QUIC transport yet), proxy configurations are kept (connections go direct), endpoints have no signatures, and `nw_listener_create_with_connection` returns NULL (no QUIC streams). | The iOS 26 Swift API: `NetworkConnection` / `NetworkChannel` (`start()`, `state`, `onStateUpdate`, `onPathUpdate`, `onViabilityUpdate`, `onBetterPathUpdate`, endpoints, `currentPath`; `send` / `receive(exactly:)` / `receive(atLeast:atMost:)` on streams, `send` / `receive()` on datagrams, WebSocket text, binary, `ping`, `pong`, `close`, TLV `send(_:type:)`, Coder `send(_:)`, `messages`), `withNetworkConnection(to:using:_:)`, `NetworkListener` (`run`, `port`, `service`, `newConnectionLimit`, state and service registration updates), `NetworkBrowser` (`run` with `RunResult`), `ListenerProvider.bonjour` / `BonjourListenerProvider`, `BrowserProvider.bonjour` / `Bonjour.Endpoint`, `Connectable`; the stack builders `IP`, `TCP`, `UDP`, `TLS` (ALPN, versions, local identity, `certificateValidator`), `WebSocket`, `TLV`, `Coder` (`NetworkCoder` `.json`, `.propertyList`), `NWParametersBuilder` and the `NWParametersProvider` modifiers, `NetworkProtocolOptions` and its marker protocols, `UnexpectedEndpointType` | ✅ | 26.0 | adapted: over isim's `NWConnection`, `NWListener` and `NWBrowser` (host sockets, OpenSSL, isim's Bonjour registry). TLV puts a big-endian type and length (UInt32 each by default) before the value; Coder frames each message with a 4-byte length on streams (one datagram per message on UDP), so isim peers interoperate with each other. A refused connection waits (`.waiting`), as `NWConnection` does, until it is ready or its task is cancelled. `NWParametersBuilder` takes one protocol stack (Apple's variadic form crashes isim's Swift 6.2 compiler). Also: `DTLS` stacks (iOS 27), `Framer` stacks (the app's framer as the one message protocol of the connection), `receive(as:)` / `send` of network-order integers, WebSocket `startSend` / `startReceive` (messages in pieces), the TLS cipher-suite modifiers and `IP.localAddressPreference`. Not on isim: QUIC streams and datagrams (isim's QUIC is a stub), Wi-Fi Aware, Apple's variadic `ProtocolStackBuilder.buildBlock(_:_:)`. Tested (HelloConnections `-structured`, tests/ui/test_connections.py `test_connections_structured`, `os_matrix`) |
| Wi-Fi Aware (`NWParameters.wifiAware`, `NWEndpoint.wifiAware`, `NWPath.wifiAware`, `NetworkConnection.wifiAware`, `BrowserProvider` / `ListenerProvider.wifiAware`, `kNWErrorDomainWiFiAware` aside) | ❌ | 26.0 | not implemented: these use the WiFiAware framework's types (`WAParameters`, `WAEndpoint`, `WAPath`, `WAConnection`), which isim does not have yet |
